title: Someone new to flowweb.app names their business on first sign-in, and someone with an invite link joins the right account after signing in or up
description: The Owner wants to hand FlowWeb to friends and add people to a business or a flow. With open sign-up (FW-C-081) a brand-new person signs in to nothing, and an invite link (/join/<token>, made by the accounts work) has no page. Add packages/web/src/home/firstRun.tsx: NameBusiness asks for the business name (autocomplete organization), calls createAccount(name) from hosted/auth.ts and hands back the new account; JoinInvite calls acceptInvite(token) once and says the person is in, or shows our own sentence when the link is used up or wrong. inviteFromPath reads the token from /join/<token>, and rememberInvite / pendingInvite / clearInvite keep it in sessionStorage across the sign-in or Google round trip. A signed-out visitor on an invite link sees the homepage with a line saying they were invited. App.tsx, once signed in, accepts a pending invite first, then shows NameBusiness when listAccounts() is empty. No backend here: the auth and account calls come from hosted/auth.ts. No em dashes in the copy.
acceptance: NameBusiness shows a heading Name your business and a field with autocomplete organization; submitting calls createAccount with the trimmed name and then onDone with the result; a blank name calls nothing
A createAccount error shows in an alert
JoinInvite calls acceptInvite(token) exactly once, then says you are in and calls onJoined with the account id; a failure shows in an alert with a way on to FlowWeb
inviteFromPath('/join/<token>') returns the token and returns null for other paths; rememberInvite, pendingInvite and clearInvite keep it across a reload in sessionStorage
HomePage with an invite shows that the visitor was invited
